title: On Light, Absence, and the Space Between
bio: Sample Artist is a multidisciplinary practitioner whose work traverses painting, installation, and digital media. Based between London and Tokyo, their practice investigates the phenomenology of attention — how the eye lingers, hesitates, and ultimately fails to grasp.

content.text: Your recent work seems preoccupied with what is absent from the frame rather than what is present. Is that a conscious decision?

It becomes conscious only in retrospect. While I am working, I am following a kind of pressure — a sense that something in the composition is pulling toward an edge, wanting to leave. I follow that pressure. The empty space is never planned; it arrives.
There is a quality of restraint in the work — almost an ethical restraint. Where does that come from?

I think it comes from distrust of spectacle. I grew up in an environment saturated with images that demanded emotional responses they had not earned. I became suspicious of that demand. The work I make now tries to earn its moment very slowly, if at all.
How do you know when a work is finished?
When I stop being able to improve it and start only being able to change it. That is a different feeling entirely — from refinement to revision. Once I cross that threshold I leave the studio.
